I am a Senior Research Fellow in the [Department of Information Studies](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/information-studies), [University College London (UCL)](https://www.ucl.ac.uk). I&nbsp;work across computational social science and population data science. [<svg aria-hidden="true" width="0.9em" height="0.9em" viewBox="0 0 16 16" style="vertical-align:-0.1em" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><circle cx="8" cy="8" r="7.2"/><path d="M4.6 8h6.4M8.4 5.2 11.2 8l-2.8 2.8"/></svg>&nbsp;*See my UCL profile.*](https://profiles.ucl.ac.uk/99917-andreas-mastrosavvas){.text-nowrap}

My research examines how people's social, economic and political outcomes relate to the places and networks they are part of. This includes work on [the geography of partisan homophily in online social ties](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apgeog.2024.103371), on [the political spillovers of local economic shocks through social networks](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.regsciurbeco.2024.104024) and on the relationship between [remote work and internal migration](https://events.rdmobile.com/Lists/Details/3428931). I&nbsp;also develop methods, tools and resources, such as the [Longitudinal Impossible Dataset](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/population-health-sciences/epidemiology-health-care/research/ucl-research-department-epidemiology-public-health/research/health-and-social-surveys-research-group/studies/celsius/longitudinal-impossible-dataset), that make population data easier to use safely in social science research.

I have wide-ranging experience with census, survey, administrative and digital trace data (and their metadata). I&nbsp;am a member of the [Census Service](https://ukdataservice.ac.uk/learning-hub/census/) at the [UK Data Service](https://ukdataservice.ac.uk) and have previously worked at [UCL CeLSIUS](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/population-health-sciences/epidemiology-health-care/research/ucl-research-department-epidemiology-public-health/research/health-and-social-surveys-research-group/studies/celsius), the [Office for National Statistics](https://www.ons.gov.uk) and the [Welsh Government](https://www.gov.wales).

I [teach](https://profiles.ucl.ac.uk/99917-andreas-mastrosavvas/teaching) quantitative and computational methods to multidisciplinary student cohorts, and have taught students in sociology, politics, geography, epidemiology and digital humanities.
